body:
Popular brands are widely imitated. Fake devices and liquids look convincing in photos, can sell for tempting prices and may perform poorly, leak or have unreliable battery and coil quality. For you as a buyer, the risk is not only wasted money: an imitation product may not meet the rules, may carry no proper warnings and may be built with unknown components. This guide explains the warning signs of a counterfeit, how to check packaging, how verification codes work, why required warnings matter, what to look for in weight and feel, how to judge a seller, what to do if you suspect a fake and how to reduce your risk when you shop. It is general information for adults aged 21 and over, not legal advice. Nicotine is addictive.

## Why counterfeits exist
Brands that sell well attract imitators. A convincing copy can be made cheaply and sold at a discount, or at the normal price to buyers who cannot tell the difference. Counterfeits are most common with high-demand disposables, because they are cheap to copy and sell fast. Imitation is not limited to unknown sellers: it can appear in marketplaces, on social media and sometimes in shops that do not check their supply. The best protection is knowing what to look for and buying from sellers who explain where their products come from.

## Price that is too good
A price far below the usual market range is a red flag. Compare across reputable retailers and see [how to compare vape prices](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/). A genuine product has a cost floor, and a seller cannot sell much below it for long without a reason. If a device sells for a fraction of its usual price, ask why. A discount that looks too good is often a sign of a copy, stolen stock or old stock that has expired.

## Packaging details
Look for sharp printing, correct spelling, consistent fonts and clean seals. Compare with images on the brand's official site. Poor printing, color mismatches, typos, blurry logos or glue marks suggest a fake. Check that the box closes neatly, that the plastic wrap is applied evenly and that the information on the box matches the device. Look at details such as batch numbers and dates, which should be clear and consistent. A genuine product's packaging is usually uniform from one unit to the next.

## Verification codes
Many brands include a code or QR on the package that links to a verification page. Use the brand's official domain, typed yourself, not a link from a message or an unfamiliar site, because scammers copy verification pages too. A code that does not work, that has been used many times or that leads to a page that does not look official is a concern. Some brands do not offer verification, so the absence of a code is not proof of a fake, but the presence of one that fails is a warning.

## Required warnings
U.S. packaging should carry the FDA nicotine warning: "WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical." Missing or incorrectly worded warnings are a concern. So is packaging in another language only, with no English labeling. A product that does not meet labeling rules may not have been made for the U.S. market, and it may have been imported illegally. See [what the nicotine warning label means](/blog/what-the-nicotine-warning-label-means/).

## Weight and feel
Fakes may feel lighter, because they use smaller batteries or less liquid, or heavier because of cheaper parts. They may have rough seams, loose parts, an uneven finish or buttons that feel wrong. Check for flavor or nicotine strength inconsistent with the label, a harsh or chemical taste, leaking out of the box, or a battery that dies far sooner than the specification suggests. If you have used a genuine unit of the same product, compare them. These signs are not proof on their own, but several together are a strong indication.

### Performance clues
- **Battery that drains in a fraction of the expected time.**
- **Flavor that is weak, odd or inconsistent with the label.**
- **Leaking when new,** which can mean a poor seal.
- **A device that fails or flickers** soon after first use.
- **A heat or smell that is unusual.**

If you see any of these, stop using the device and contact the seller.

## The seller
Buy from a retailer with clear contact details, published [shipping](/shipping/) and [refund](/refunds/) policies and a real business address. Look for an explanation of how it sources products, adult-signature delivery, and age checks. Avoid social-media sellers with no history, sellers that will not tell you where they are, sellers that skip age verification and sellers that offer prices that do not make sense. A seller that follows the rules for remote sales is more likely to deal in genuine products, because it has more to lose.

### What we do
We source from manufacturer and authorized distribution channels, we list products with their brand, strength and specifications, we publish our shipping and returns policies and we require adult signature on every parcel. If you have a doubt about a product you received from us, contact us with photos and your order ID, and we will look into it. See [how to contact support](/blog/how-to-contact-support/).

## What to do if you suspect a fake
Stop using it, keep the packaging and contact the seller. Take clear photos of the packaging, the label, any codes and the device. Note where and when you bought it, and keep your receipt. If the product was bought from us, email with your order ID, and we will review it. If it was bought elsewhere, contact that seller, and consider reporting a suspected counterfeit to the brand through its official channels. Learn about [disposal](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/) if the device is damaged.

## Reducing your risk
- **Buy from sellers you can identify,** with clear policies.
- **Compare prices** before you buy, and be wary of big discounts.
- **Check the packaging** against the brand's official images.
- **Use official verification pages,** typing the address yourself.
- **Keep your order records** so you can report a problem.
- **Do not use a device that looks or behaves oddly.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can a counterfeit be dangerous?
Imitations may use unknown components and may not meet the standards of the genuine product. A damaged or poorly made battery is a particular concern. Stop using a suspect device, and follow the guidance in [lithium battery care basics](/blog/lithium-battery-care-basics-for-vapes/).

### Is every cheap product fake?
No. Sales and clearance exist. But a price far below the usual range, with no explanation, deserves a second look.

### Can I check a product myself?
Compare it with the brand's official images, check the warning and the labeling, use any official verification page and note the weight and finish. If you are unsure, ask the seller.

### What if the seller will not respond?
Keep your records, contact your payment provider if appropriate and report the product to the brand. Be more careful with that seller in future.

### Do you guarantee that products are genuine?
We make no absolute claims, but we source from manufacturer and authorized distribution channels and will review any product you doubt.

## A worked example: comparing two listings
You see the same disposable listed at two prices: $19.99 at a retailer with a business address, a clear returns policy and adult-signature delivery, and $9.99 on a social media account with no address and no policy. The cheaper listing has photos with a different font on the box. You check the brand's official site and see that the font on the box differs from the official images. You decide not to buy from the cheaper seller, because the price, the lack of information and the packaging all point the same way. A few minutes of comparison save you from a poor product and a lost payment.

## Keeping evidence
If you buy a product you later suspect is not genuine, keep the box, the device, any inserts, the receipt and the tracking information. Photograph everything from several angles, including batch numbers and codes. Evidence helps the seller investigate, helps the brand identify counterfeits and helps you if you need to dispute a payment. Do not throw the packaging away until the matter is resolved.

## Helping others
If you spot a counterfeit, tell the brand through its official channels, and warn friends who buy the same product. Counterfeit sellers rely on people not noticing or not speaking up, and every report makes their job harder. Be careful not to accuse a specific seller publicly without evidence, and stick to facts.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I tell a counterfeit from a photo alone?
Sometimes, but photos can be copied, and fakes can look identical online. Check how the seller describes the product, whether it explains its sourcing and whether its policies look real. The physical product tells you more when it arrives.

### Does a missing QR code mean a fake?
Not always. Some brands do not include codes. But a code that fails, or leads to an unfamiliar site, is a warning.

### What if I bought it from a shop in person?
The same checks apply. Reputable shops can be deceived by bad supply, so check the packaging and warnings, keep your receipt and tell the shop if something looks wrong.
